description: The Asian Development Bank produces Multiregional Input-Output (MRIO) tables that show how the industries of Asian and Pacific economies buy from and sell to each other and the rest of the world. The page of the Key Indicators Database read on 2026-09-28 explains that the tables build on the World Input-Output Database to cover 29 Asia and Pacific economies, that ADB compiles tables at current prices for 62 and 72 economies plus an aggregated rest of the world, with more recent tables covering 74 economies, and that the economies identified account for at least 93% of world GDP; files are offered year by year from 2000 and from 2007 onwards, with a 71-economy series including Latin America for 2007, 2011 and 2017, alongside constant-price tables, environmentally extended tables for air emissions and global value chain indicators. Coverage is global with Asian detail. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): ADB terms of use: data may be copied, adapted and redistributed for commercial and non-commercial purposes at no cost, with attribution to ADB. Caveats: sector detail is coarse (industry level), editions differ in economy lists, and years lag by one to two years. It supports cascading failure and supply-chain disruption modelling, such as inoperability input-output analysis of infrastructure outages across borders. Related records: data-ide-jetro-asian-international-input-output-tables, data-eurostat-figaro and data-exiobase are comparable inter-country tables.
